graphs.name: FunctionLibrary::|Update Foot Post Solve
comments: If toe is colliding with floor, bring it up and aim foot

We are using pythagoras to solve for the correct toe position on the floor. B^2 = L^2 - A^2, where L is the foot to toe length, A is the foot to toe in direction of ground plane and B is the foot to toe along the ground. To do this we need to decompose the foot to toe into 2 perpendicular directions, one along ground normal and the other perpendicular to ground

graphs.name: FunctionLibrary::|UpdateRootDamper
comments: Account for ground movement
Handle fading in / out of the effect via the alpha

Translate the current damped z by the global displacement along the current ground plane. This is done so that the global z damper doesn't pull is down into slopes when walking up them. We only want to see its effects along the ground normal, not perpendicular to it
Apply Damper to root bone (need to convert to component space)
Update the smoother

The purpose of the root damper is to smooth out any discontinuity coming from the movement component. For example when moving up a ledge / curb or falling down a small ledge, we don't want the character to 'pop' down. This effect is done in world space, unlike the pelvis offset.

Important: we don't want this damper to change the animated result when moving up a constant slope, so we only damp in the direction of the ground normal.

In order for this to work properly the correct ground normal must be fed in from the movement component.
